120 minutes for everything you submit, including your video, as stated on the cover.

### The situation

SidelineReel is Ajaia's app for youth sports clubs and leagues. A coach uploads full game footage, or sets up a sideline camera to record it automatically. SidelineReel finds each kid's highlight moments, goals, saves, big plays, cuts them into a personal reel for that kid, and assembles a weekly team recap it sends to every family on the roster. Customers are clubs and leagues who pay for a season. Users are the coaches who upload footage and the parents who watch and share the reels.

You are the Product Manager for SidelineReel. You do not write the production code and you do not decide the visual design. You decide what gets built next, why, and what the spec asks the team to build.

**Roster tagging:** the step where SidelineReel matches a jersey number in the footage to a name on the team roster, so the right highlight lands in the right kid's reel.

**Auto-recap:** the weekly team video SidelineReel assembles and sends to every family on the roster on its own, without a coach or parent building it by hand.

### The materials

**Material 1. Email, Carla Reyes, Executive Director, Ridgeline Youth Soccer Club, this morning, subject "We need livestreaming locked in before signups"**

> SidelineReel's highlight reels are a big part of why half our parents renewed this year, genuinely. But our board wants more: live streaming of every game, not just the highlight clips afterward, so grandparents and college scouts can watch in real time. I've raised this with your sales team twice already. Ridgeline is your biggest club account and our season renewal and signups open in six weeks. I need to know if this is on your roadmap before I talk to my board.
>
> Carla

**Material 2. Product research summary, compiled by the SidelineReel research lead, this week**

> **Quarterly parent survey (210 respondents across 40 clubs):** "More editing controls, so I can trim my kid's reel and add my own music" was the top requested improvement, named by 58% of respondents as their single biggest ask.
>
> **Usage data, last 90 days, all accounts:** the Share button on the weekly auto-recap is used in 90% of recaps sent. The Reel Editor, the feature respondents asked for more of, was opened by 6% of parents in the same window, and fewer than 1% of the parents who opened it finished an edit.

>
> **Filed by a coach at a club, this week.** "When I save a reel straight to my phone's camera roll, the team logo watermark is sometimes missing in the corner. Not urgent, just noticed it."

**Material 4. Slack, #sidelinereel-gtm, Jamal Whitfield, VP of Sales, yesterday, 5:10 PM**

**Material 5. SidelineReel Weekly Product Health, internal dashboard snapshot, this week**

> **Reel Share Rate: 92%** (reels shared to at least one other person, calculated only over reels a parent opened)
>

Most of those sit unopened because the notification arrives late at night, or because the reel's thumbnail shows the wrong kid, which support tickets suggest happens most often when jersey numbers are visually similar.

### Tasks

**Task 1. The roadmap call** (suggested time: 30 minutes)

Using Materials 1 through 5, decide what SidelineReel builds next. Rank the candidates for the roadmap, evidence-based. Name at least one thing you would NOT build next and why, including livestreaming for Ridgeline if that is your call.

**Task 2. The spec** (suggested time: 35 minutes)

Write the spec for the top item on your roadmap. Include: the outcome it is meant to produce, what is explicitly in and out of scope, where a human stays in the loop, acceptance criteria someone could test, and the top two ways this could fail once it ships and what would catch each one.

**Task 3. Build a working prototype** (suggested time: 35 minutes)

Build a working prototype of the core flow for the top item on your roadmap: the two or three screens or steps that matter. It has to run or click, an AI-built app (v0, Lovable, Replit, Bolt, Claude, or any tool of your choice), a clickable prototype, or working code. Static frames alone are not the task. Submit it as a working link or a runnable file.

**Task 4. AI Workflow Note** (suggested time: 5 minutes)

In a few sentences: which tasks above you used AI for, what you deliberately kept human, and one specific thing an AI tool got wrong or you chose not to use.

### Your video

One video (suggested time: 15 minutes inside the 120-minute window; aim for 5 to 10 minutes of recording). Screen plus camera. Walk through your roadmap call from Task 1 and your spec from Task 2, and demo the prototype from Task 3 running. Close by telling us who you are, why this role and why Ajaia, and your salary expectations for this role. Do not state your current compensation; we are not asking for it here or anywhere else in this process.
